}}'''Yōichirō Suzuki''' ({{langx|ja|鈴木 洋一郎}}, born 1952) is a Japanese experimental particle physicist, notable for his work on [[neutrino]]s. 

==Early life==
Suzuki was born and grew up in Tokyo. His father was a tailor.<ref name="AIP2015"/>

==Career==
Suzuki earned his Ph.D. in physics from [[Kyoto University|Kyōto University]] in 1979 under Kozo Miyake.<ref name="AIP2015">{{cite web | title=Yoichiro Suzuki | website=American Institute of Physics | date=28 April 2015 | url=https://www.aip.org/history-programs/niels-bohr-library/oral-histories/23109 | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> After postdoctoral work at [[Brown University|Brown]] and [[Osaka University]], he was appointed associate professor at the [[Institute for Cosmic Ray Research]] (ICRR) at [[University of Tokyo|Tōkyō University]] in 1989. He was promoted to professor in 1996 and became director of the institute in 2004.<ref name="jspsusa.org">{{cite web | title=Bio.Yoichiro.Suzuki | website=jspsusa.org | url=http://www.jspsusa.org/FORUM2005/bio.suzuki.htm | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> Suzuki was deputy director of the [[Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]] (IPMU) at Tōkyō University from 2007 until March 2018.<ref name="IPMU">{{cite web| title=Yoichiro Suzuki| website=Kavli IPMU| url=https://db.ipmu.jp/member/personal/786en.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> In addition, he has been director of the [[Kamioka]] observatory since 2002.<ref name="ICRR">{{cite web | title=ICRR / About ICRR | website=ICRR| url=http://www.icrr.u-tokyo.ac.jp/material/daih_e.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>

==Awards==
During the 1990s, Suzuki was spokesperson and project leader for the [[Super Kamiokande]] collaboration that demonstrated [[neutrino oscillation]]. For these achievements he received the [[Asahi Prize]] in 1999 (as part of the Super Kamiokande team),<ref name="Asahi">{{cite web | author=The Asahi Shimbun Company | title=The Asahi Prize - English Information | website=The Asahi Shimbun Company | url=http://www.asahi.com/shimbun/award/asahi/english.html | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>  the [[Nishina Memorial Prize]] in 2001,<ref name="nishina">{{cite web | title=Nishina Memorial Prize| website=nishina-mf.or.jp| date=18 December 2013| url=http://www.nishina-mf.or.jp/NishinaMemorialPrize-E.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> the [[Bruno Pontecorvo Prize]] in 2010,<ref name="Pontecorvo">{{cite web| title=Bruno Pontecorvo Prize to Yoichiro Suzuki| website=Kavli IPMU| date=16 February 2011| url=https://www.ipmu.jp/ja/node/967| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> and the [[European Physical Society|EPS]] [[Cocconi Prize]] in 2013 (with [[Arthur B. McDonald]]).<ref name="EPS2013">{{cite web| title=The Giuseppe and Vanna Cocconi Prize for Particle Astrophysics and Cosmology is awarded to Prof. Yoichiro Suzuki| website=Kamioka Observatory| date=14 May 2013| url=http://www-sk.icrr.u-tokyo.ac.jp/whatsnew/new-20130514-e.html| access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref> In 2016, Suzuki and the Super Kamiokande team were awarded the [[Breakthrough Prize in Fundamental Physics]] together with other neutrino research consortia.<ref name="Breakthrough Prize 2016">{{cite web | title=Breakthrough Prize – Fundamental Physics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Yoichiro Suzuki and the Super K Collaboration | website=Breakthrough Prize | date=1 October 2016 | url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/1/L150 | access-date=20 September 2018}}</ref>
